headline: Synonym Showdown: Find Stronger Words as a Team
problemStatement: A synonym list is most useful when learners can compare choices in context and discover how meaning changes with register or precision. Synonym Showdown gives the class a target word and its context sentence, then asks students to produce alternatives and explain which ones fit.
outcomes: Expand active vocabulary by producing multiple synonyms for a target word.
Compare word quality and context instead of assuming every similar word is interchangeable.
Use a final speaking prompt to put a selected synonym into an original sentence.
howItWorks: The game generates a target word with a context sentence. Students submit synonym ideas on their phones during a race.
Each distinct suggestion is checked once, while each student's list is tracked separately. One student's word does not block another learner from earning credit for it.
Accepted answers show their points and quality; rejected words show a reason. A word found by only one student earns a rare-word bonus.
At the end, the class sees a word wall with unique discoveries marked and can complete the Use it in a sentence speaking beat.
teacherUseCases: Choose a familiar target when students need confidence, or use unit vocabulary to reinforce a current topic.
Compare a basic synonym with a rarer option and ask which one sounds most natural in the original sentence.

faq.q: Can the same synonym count for multiple students?
faq.a: Yes. The game checks each distinct word once but tracks student lists separately, so one learner's answer does not prevent another person from earning credit.
A valid synonym earns an extra bonus when only one student found it. The word wall marks that discovery so the class can discuss why it fits.
The checker returns a quality and feedback for each answer. Accepted suggestions receive points, while unsuitable words are crossed out with a reason.
The class reviews the collected word wall, with unique discoveries highlighted, then students use a selected synonym in an original sentence.
